title: Ethiopian Honey Wine
community: All of Ethiopia — the ancient honey wine
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Tej — the ancient honey wine of Ethiopia. Raw honey dissolved in water with gesho twigs (or hops) and fermented for 2 weeks. See ETH095 for the complete recipe and heritage. This entry covers the tej house (tej bet) tradition and serving culture.
longDesc: Tej has been Ethiopia's primary alcoholic drink since before recorded history — mentioned in ancient Ethiopian chronicles, served at imperial courts, and still served today in tej houses (tej bets) throughout the country. The tej bet is the Ethiopian equivalent of a wine bar — the place where tej is served in berele (flask-shaped glasses), alongside grilled meats and conversation.
ingredients: // See ETH095 for the complete Tej recipe
// Gesho is available at Ethiopian specialty stores
equipment: Large glass or clay fermentation vessel
steps: See ETH095 for the full Tej brewing method.
Serve in berele — the distinctive flask-shaped glass unique to tej service.
Tej ranges from very sweet (short ferment, low alcohol) to dry (long ferment, high alcohol).
Traditional tej house: tej is served in the original berele, accompanied by grilled meat and awaze.
chefTips: Gesho is the defining ingredient — without it, it is honey wine, not tej.
The berele glass is the cultural vessel — drinking tej from a regular glass loses something.
commonMistakes: Substituting hops for gesho changes the character completely.
cookingScience: See ETH095 for full Tej science.
sustainabilityTips: Ethiopian mountain honey from traditional log hives — the most sustainable honey tradition.
servedWith: At tej houses alongside grilled meat
storage: Sealed vessel refrigerated after desired fermentation.
healthBenefits: Raw honey compounds survive partial fermentation.
Gesho provides bitterness and antimicrobial effect.
culturalNote: The Ethiopian tej house (tej bet) is one of Africa's most distinctive social institutions — low tables, small berele glasses, the smell of honey wine and charcoal-grilled meat, and conversations that run for hours. Tej is not consumed quickly — it is sipped slowly over the course of an evening, and the quality of the tej tells you the quality of the establishment. Emperor Haile Selassie served tej at his court; today it is served in the same berele glasses in tej bets from Addis Ababa to Gondar.
